install.packages("fortunes")

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(gt)

rhinovirus <- read_csv("data/ukhsa-chart-download-rhinovirus.csv")

gt(head(rhinovirus))
```

```{r}
weather <- read_csv("data/weather_data.csv")
ggplot(weather)
ggplot(weather, aes(
  x = observation_time,
  y = temperature_c
))
ggplot(weather, aes(
  x = observation_time,
  y = temperature_c
)) +
  geom_line()
ggplot(weather, aes(
  x = observation_time,
  y = temperature_c
)) +
  geom_line(colour = "red") +
  xlab("Date") +
  ylab("Temp (C)") +
  ggtitle("Temperature by Date")
```

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(gt)

antibiotics <- read_csv("data/ukhsa-chart-antibiotics.csv")
ggplot(antibiotics)
ggplot(antibiotics, aes(
  x = date,
  y = metric_value
)) + 
  geom_line(colour = "purple") +
  xlab("Year") +
  ylab("Standard consumption (DID)") +
  ggtitle("Standard consumption by year")

```

## Quarto

Quarto enables you to weave together content and executable code into a finished document. To learn more about Quarto see <https://quarto.org>.

## Running Code

When you click the **Render** button a document will be generated that includes both content and the output of embedded code. You can embed code like this:

```{r}
1 + 1
```

You can add options to executable code like this 

```{r}
#| echo: false
2 * 2
```

The `echo: false` option disables the printing of code (only output is displayed).
